title: Sukuk bond for 25 roads
source: investors, through the Debt Management Office
summary: Nigeria's first government Sukuk raised ₦100 billion from investors in 2017 to build or repair 25 roads. Each of the six zones received about ₦16.67 billion. We have found 15 of the 25 roads so far.
simple: In 2017 the government borrowed ₦100 billion from investors through a Sukuk (an Islamic bond) to fix 25 roads, shared equally between the six zones. We have found 15 of the roads so far.

verdict.text: About ₦16.67 billion went to each of the 6 zones
We have found 15 of the 25 roads so far. Help us find the rest.

gaps: We have found 15 of the 25 roads, from one published list. The full official list, with an amount for each road, would fill this gap.
We have not yet checked the current state of each road. If you use one of these roads, send an update.
We have not yet found an official report on the state of each Sukuk road.

timeline.text: The DMO issues a ₦100 billion, 7-year Ijarah Sukuk at 16.47% a year.
The proceeds are handed to the Ministry of Power, Works & Housing, about ₦16.67 billion per zone.
The Sukuk is listed on the Nigerian Stock Exchange and FMDQ.

nodes.label: Investors who bought the Sukuk bond
nodes.simple: Investors lent the government ₦100 billion through a Sukuk, a bond that follows Islamic finance rules.
nodes.description: A 7-year Ijarah Sukuk issued on 26 September 2017 at a 16.47% annual rental rate. It was issued through a special purpose vehicle, FGN Roads Sukuk Company 1 Plc. It was the first of several road-financing Sukuk issues.

evidence.title: DMO lists N100bn sovereign sukuk on NSE, FMDQ

nodes.label: Federal Ministry of Works
nodes.simple: The Works Ministry received the money to fix 25 roads.
nodes.description: Received the proceeds to fund 25 road projects across the six zones. Reported projects include sections of the Enugu–Port Harcourt road.

nodes.label: North Central roads
nodes.simple: About ₦16.67 billion. Roads named so far: Loko–Oweto Bridge; Abuja–Lokoja road (Sections 1 and 4); Suleja–Minna road (Phase 2); Lokoja–Benin road (Section 1).
nodes.description: About ₦16.67 billion went to this zone. A list published in October 2017 names these projects: Loko–Oweto Bridge; Abuja–Lokoja road (Sections 1 and 4); Suleja–Minna road (Phase 2); Lokoja–Benin road (Section 1). That list gives only 15 of the 25 roads, and it does not give an amount for each road. We have not yet checked the current state of each road.
